extraction.name: EuroSAT
extraction.description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 13 spectral bands and consisting out of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images.
extraction.creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors downloaded Sentinel-2A satellite images of European cities via Amazon S3, specifically selecting images with low cloud levels recorded throughout the year. From these, they extracted and manually checked 27,000 georeferenced and labeled image patches measuring 64x64 pixels.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-spectral satellite imagery from the Sentinel-2A satellite, which captures the Earth's surface using a Multi-spectral Imager (MSI) covering 13 different spectral bands with a spatial resolution of up to 10 meters per pixel.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Image patches were extracted based on satellite images and then manually checked to ensure correct labeling. The class definitions and relationships were based on the mapping guide of the European Urban Atlas.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset relies on 64x64 image patches, which limits the classification system from performing finely graduated per-pixel segmentation.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and resulting models have positive social and environmental implications, particularly for urban area development, nature protection, sustainable development, and monitoring climate change contributors like deforestation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training deep neural networks for satellite image classification, specifically for land use and land cover classification, change detection, and assisting in updating geographical maps.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were sampled from throughout the entire year to maximize variance within the land use and land cover classes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Satellite images were filtered to select those with low cloud levels. The images were then processed into 64x64 pixel georeferenced patches and manually checked.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: While a classiﬁcation system trained with 64x64 image patches does not allow a ﬁnely graduated per-pixel segmentation, it cannot only detect changes as shown in the previous examples, it can also facilitate keeping maps up-to-date.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The presented examples are particularly of interest in urban area development, nature protection or sustainable development. For instance, deforestation is a main contributor to climate change, therefore the detection of deforested land is of particular interest (e.g., to notice illegal clearing of forests).

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We provide this work in the context of the recently published EuroSAT dataset, which can be used similar to [18] as a basis for a large-scale training of deep neural networks for the task of satellite image classiﬁcation. [...] We show land use and land cover change detection applications as well as how the the trained classiﬁer can assist in keeping geographical maps up-to-date.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Furthermore, we have extracted images recorded all over the year to get a variance as high as possible inherent in the covered land use and land cover classes.
